content.text:
Two relations are available.

  corpus      one row per document in the working sample, WITH the text.
  corpus_meta one row per document in the whole corpus, WITHOUT the text.

Columns (identical in both, except `text`, which only `corpus` has):
  id                    document identifier
  text                  document text (corpus only)
  url, domain           source URL and its host
  dump, date            crawl the document came from, and its timestamp
  language              language label assigned by the corpus pipeline
  language_score        the pipeline's confidence in that label
  minhash_cluster_size  size of the near-duplicate cluster the document
                        represented before deduplication (1 = unique)
  fasttext, langdetect  labels from two independent off-the-shelf language
                        identifiers, shipped with the corpus release
  lingua_top            top language from a third identifier, which reports
                        a distribution over languages within the document
  lingua_top_p          that identifier's proportion for lingua_top
  n_bad_words           number of profanity-list matches recorded by the
                        corpus release
  n_chars, n_words, n_lines  document size
Raw pipeline fields `top_langs` (JSON) and `lingua` (list of
(language, proportion) pairs, as text) are also available on both
relations if you want the full distributions.

corpus_meta: 26,470,482 documents (full corpus)

input.description: A single machine-generated SEO spam network hosted on Google Firebase Hosting (*.web.app and *.firebaseapp.com) supplies 1.41M documents (5.3% of docs, 12.3% of all words). Pages are not Slovak prose but concatenations of unrelated scraped snippets (Slovak, Czech, English, Swedish, Hindi transliteration) under a keyword-stuffed title, on ~2,800 throwaway hosts whose names are a Swedish/Slovak money keyword plus a random 4-letter suffix (hurmanblirrik*, kopavguld*, enklapengar*, akozbohatnut*, iahkepeniaze*, lon*, casino*, torrents*).
input.selector: domain LIKE '%.web.app' OR domain LIKE '%.firebaseapp.com'
input.evidence:
Aggregates: 1,408,437/26,470,482 docs (5.32%) and 12.29% of all n_words in corpus_meta; 823 firebaseapp.com hosts + 1,972 web.app hosts. Mean length ~1,000 words, mean minhash_cluster_size 1.002 — so near-duplicate dedup did NOT remove them (every page is a unique random snippet mix). Mean lingua_top_p is 0.70 vs 0.82 corpus-wide, consistent with multi-source splicing. I inspected 13 documents from these hosts (5 random, 8 via evaluate_detector on the selector, 1 full read of <urn:uuid:e524965f...>); 13/13 were the spam pattern, with zero legitimate Firebase-hosted Slovak sites seen. The full read shows a page titled 'Darčeková karta' splicing Amazon/BitPay/Revolut English marketing copy, Swedish donation text, Hindi-in-Latin bitcoin spam and unrelated Slovak bank T&Cs, ending in a raw keyword list. Listing the lowest-count hosts (all c=1) shows the same generated-name pattern, so there is no legitimate long tail on these two suffixes. Counter-evidence: the pipeline is not obviously wrong to call the pages Slovak — Slovak is usually the plurality language (94.5% have lingua_top='sk'), and language_score averages 0.98; the defect is that the text is incoherent spliced spam, not that the label is wrong.</evidence>
<parameter name="expected_precision">0.99
input.likely_false_positives: A genuine small Slovak site that happens to be hosted on Firebase Hosting; none appeared in 13 inspections or in the host-name listing.

input.description: The corpus text was silently rewritten by a PII scrubber that replaced essentially every e-mail address with one of two English placeholder strings ("email@example.com" or "firstname.lastname@example.org"). ~3.7% of documents carry these injected tokens, the real addresses are gone, and the redaction is inconsistent (phone numbers and personal names in the very same contact block are left intact).
input.selector: text LIKE '%firstname.lastname@example.org%' OR text LIKE '%email@example.com%'
input.evidence:
Free SQL over the 2,034,896-doc working sample: 76,326 documents contain any string matching an e-mail regex, and 76,133 of them (99.7%) contain one of the two placeholders — i.e. real addresses are essentially absent from the corpus. Grouping the first regex match per document gives 'firstname.lastname@example.org' 38,096 and 'email@example.com' 37,829 as the top two by three orders of magnitude; the few remaining hits are mangled strings where whitespace was lost during extraction (e.g. '[email]', 50 docs), not surviving clean addresses. run_detector: 76,133/2,034,896 = 3.74% (95% CI 3.72-3.77%), ≈990k documents extrapolated to the full corpus. I inspected 6 documents drawn by the selector: 6/6 genuinely contain an injected placeholder in a natural Slovak contact context (e-shop T&Cs, real-estate listings, company contact blocks). Document <urn:uuid:8990ac89-...> shows the inconsistency directly: agent name 'Ing. Bernardína Beneová' and phone '0908 133 421' are kept verbatim while the e-mail is replaced, so this is not effective anonymisation, only data corruption. Counter-evidence: the affected documents are otherwise fluent Slovak and useful; the defect is a localised token-level corruption plus an undocumented mutation of the source text, not whole-document garbage.</evidence>
<parameter name="expected_precision">1.0
input.likely_false_positives: A document that genuinely quoted 'email@example.com' as a documentation example (e.g. a tutorial on configuring mail); such uses exist on the web but were not seen in the 6 inspected documents.
input.assertion: Either no document contains the placeholder strings, or the release documents the e-mail substitution and applies it consistently to phone numbers and names as well.

input.selector: (length(text)-length(replace(replace(replace(text,'ř',''),'ě',''),'ů','')))::double/nullif(n_chars,0) > 0.005 AND domain NOT LIKE '%.web.app' AND domain NOT LIKE '%.firebaseapp.com'
input.evidence:
The selector keys on ř/ě/ů, three letters that exist in Czech but not in the Slovak alphabet, requiring them to make up >0.5% of characters (roughly one Czech-only letter per 200 chars, i.e. a running Czech passage rather than a stray quoted word). Free SQL on the 2,034,896-doc sample: 237,560 docs (11.7%) contain at least one such letter, 41,267 (2.03%) exceed the 0.5% density, and 23,076 (1.13%, ≈300k full-corpus) do so outside the Firebase spam farm. Metadata cross-check: 114,525 docs (0.43%) have BOTH independent LIDs (fasttext and langdetect) saying 'cs'; language_score bins show that in the 0.7 bin 70% of docs are fasttext='cs' while in the 1.0 bin only 0.6% are, so the pipeline's own confidence does register the problem but its threshold does not exclude them. I inspected 16 documents in this space. The pages are machine-generated: Slovak dating/porn keyword-spam with deliberately character-scrambled words ("rádioaktíbne", "Odpovďe", "kúpeľbá", "oZznamka") to defeat duplicate detection, or machine-translated Russian/English lifestyle articles. 473,571 documents (1.79%) across ~6,500 hosts.
input.selector: domain NOT LIKE '%.sk' AND domain NOT LIKE '%.cz' AND regexp_matches(url, '^https?://[^/]+/[a-z0-9-]+\.html$')
input.evidence:
The selector matches 473,571/26,470,482 docs (1.789%, exact on the full corpus) over 6,466 hosts; the top hosts each contribute 4k-11k docs (40l.de 10,949; 1percentcommission.com 10,484; arabclicks.info 10,155; 2brothersmobiledetailing.com 9,294; 189795.xyz 8,393; 180145.xyz; 181275.xyz; adv-moto-girl.bike; ballyclarebid.co.uk; bacousa.com), which is not a plausible shape for a real foreign-hosted Slovak site. I inspected 18 documents from this network. evaluate_detector with n=10 returned 10/10 machine-generated junk: five Slovak dating/porn keyword-spam pages whose URL slugs are Slovak with the diacritic letters simply deleted (/datovania-vemi-plach-mu.html = 'datovania veľmi plachý muž', /mama-syn-skuton-sex-psky.html, /najlep-obrzok-pre-dtumov-daje-profil.html) and whose body text contains the same deletion/transposition corruption inside otherwise Slovak sentences; three machine-translated content-farm articles whose slugs betray the source language (kakizaki-clinic.com//allergija-na-solnce-u-detej-lechenie.html from Russian, myhometownfl.com//96-baby-for-two-children-15-examples.html and fintantaite.com//80-10-no-heat-hairstyles... from English); and two pages on free-TLD hosts with random-string names (tikkthha.ga, bhxkrkzd.ga) whose URLs are meaningless (/a15j6-ud8752-huy1-16-ey.html). n_bad_words>=20 is dominated by hosts of this network (adv-moto-girl.bike, accesslocator.net, badotea.info, babyweightmagic.com). KEY COUNTER-EVIDENCE that the URL shape alone is not the culprit: the identical URL shape restricted to .sk hosts (245,158 docs) sampled at n=5 gave 5/5 genuine Slovak pages (a Banská Bystrica events page, an e-shop product page, a recipe, a game shop, a real-estate listing), which is why the selector excludes .sk and .cz. Limitation: the selector will miss network members whose URLs are not flat .html, and it does not distinguish the keyword-spam sub-type from the machine-translation sub-type.</evidence>
<parameter name="expected_precision">0.9

input.assertion: No single non-.sk host that is not a recognised international site should contribute more than a few hundred documents to a Slovak slice.

The text is translationese with characteristic MT failures (proper nouns translated as common nouns, spaced punctuation, English/Romanian/Russian source slugs left in the URL) and is not native Slovak, yet it is labelled slk_Latn with score ≈1.0.
input.selector: domain LIKE 'sk.%' AND domain NOT LIKE '%.sk' AND domain NOT LIKE 'sk.%wikipedia.org'
input.evidence:
Exact on the full corpus: 903,273/26,470,482 docs (3.412%) over 9,716 'sk.'-prefixed non-.sk hosts; the head is sk.airbnb.com 135,347, sk.265health.com 49,901, sk.hotels.com 43,616, sk.pinterest.com 22,226, then a long tail of thousands of hosts with 2k-8k docs each (sk.myservername.com, sk.soringpcrepair.com, sk.smarthomemaking.com, sk.gautamblogs.com, sk.secrettohappypets.com, sk.woman-b.com, sk.rayhaber.com, sk.eturbonews.com, sk.news-front.info). sk.wikipedia.org / sk.m.wikipedia.org (51k docs) are excluded by the selector because they are genuine Slovak. I inspected 18 documents from this space. A blind sample of 8 (excluding the airbnb/hotels/pinterest heads) gave 8/8 machine translation; evaluate_detector on the exact selector at n=10 gave 9/10 machine-translated or non-Slovak-origin content. Direct MT evidence in the documents: sk.amtelefon.com renders 'Apple' as the fruit ('zástupcovia jablko povedal', 'nezmizne z portfólia jablko') and keeps the Romanian source slug /conform-unor-zvonuri-neoficiale-apple-va-lansa-trei-modele/; sk.265health.com has English-style spaced punctuation (' , ') and untranslated headers ('Forms', 'História'); sk.obtic.org, sk.smarthomemaking.com, sk.irlconsulist.com, sk.anymediaeditor.com and sk.myservername.com all keep English URL slugs; sk.merxmusicproductions.eu and sk.oriimec.eu additionally show Windows-1250-as-Latin-1 mojibake ('Membránové èerpadlá ... úèinnos» vïaka ¹pecifickej kon¹trukcii'). Counter-evidence: the selector does catch some legitimate material — sk.scribd.com hosts genuine Slovak university texts, sk.wikipedia is deliberately excluded, and sk.airbnb.com / sk.hotels.com / sk.pinterest.com are real localisations of international platforms whose Slovak chrome is professionally produced even if the user-generated body text is mixed-language; those heads are ~210k of the 903k documents, so precision is lower on the head than on the long tail.</evidence>
<parameter name="expected_precision">0.85

input.assertion: Documents from 'sk.'-prefixed subdomains of non-Slovak sites should be flagged as machine-translated and either excluded or shipped with a provenance tag.

input.selector: text LIKE '%Textová Inzercia%'
input.evidence:
Free SQL on the 2,034,896-doc working sample: 18,887 documents contain the marker, spread over only 3 hosts, of which zdravie.sk contributes 18,661; within the sample zdravie.sk has 27,188 documents, so 68.6% of that host's documents are affected. Counter-evidence that this is NOT a corpus-wide extraction failure: generic boilerplate markers are rare overall — a standalone "Reklama" line occurs in only 2,443 docs (0.12%), "Prihlásiť sa" in 8,645 (0.42%), a leading cookie banner in ~13,600 (0.67%) — so the extractor is generally clean and this is a host-specific template it fails on. The marker itself is unambiguous: no document I saw contains "Textová Inzercia" as genuine editorial content.</evidence>

|---|---|---|---|

| `longform_machine_translated_russian_health_farm` | metadata (n_words+domain) | 147,318 | 0.56% docs / **9.0% words** |

| `czech_text_labelled_as_slovak` | text | ~300k est. | 1.13% of sample |
| `advertising_boilerplate_spliced_into_text` | text | ~244k est. | 0.93% of sample |
| `language_score_invalid_and_uninformative` | metadata (exact) | 10,691,128 | 40.4% |

**The strongest one:** ~2,800 Google Firebase Hosting throwaway hosts (`hurmanblirrik*.web.app`, `akozbohatnut*.firebaseapp.com`, …) contribute 1.41M pages of spliced scraped-snippet salad, averaging 1,000 words each. Every page has `minhash_cluster_size = 1`, so near-duplicate dedup was structurally unable to see them. They are **24% of all words in the 2022 crawls and 31% in 2023** — the newest and largest slices of the corpus are the most contaminated.

**The most surprising one:** the corpus text has been silently mutated. 76,326 documents in the working sample contain an e-mail address and 76,133 of them contain `email@example.com` or `firstname.lastname@example.org` — real addresses are essentially absent. The redaction is also inconsistent: in one real-estate listing the agent's full name and phone number survive verbatim while the e-mail is scrubbed.

## Hypotheses I tested and rejected

- **Dedup failed.** No. In the 2M sample, 2,034,894 of 2,034,896 documents have a unique text hash. Same-URL-and-same-size copies are only 42,355 docs (0.16%) corpus-wide. 14.7% of docs do share a URL, but inspection showed these are homepages re-crawled with different headlines, i.e. legitimately different.
- **Documents contain repeated boilerplate lines.** No. Of 1.15M docs with ≥10 lines, only 42 have under 50% distinct lines — line-level dedup was clearly applied.
- **Wikipedia mirrors inflate the corpus.** No. The Wikipedia footer phrase appears in 30 `sk.wikipedia.org` docs and 13 `wikiwand.com` docs; mirroring is negligible.
- **Diacritic-stripped Slovak is widespread.** No — 0.34% of docs ≥100 words.

My `czech_text_labelled_as_slovak` precision estimate of 0.85 is probably optimistic. At the low end of the density band (0.005–0.007) I inspected 8 more documents and only about half had a clear Czech passage; the higher-density band ran 8/10. Honest overall precision is nearer 0.75–0.8.

## What I'd do with more budget

1. Build a general MT-detector rather than host lists — the `kamsi.sk`-style pseudo-Slovak ("Odporúčajeme využit **všechny** naše filtry **na základě počtu osob**") and `naj.sk` e-commerce MT are clearly systematic but I could only pin them to individual hosts.
2. Quantify PII retention properly: 2.4% of sampled docs contain a Slovak phone number and 0.65% an IČO, against a scrubber that removed only e-mails.
3. Chase two smaller networks I identified but did not size: the ~115-host farm sharing the English string *"We are searching data for your request"*, and the 5-letter `.online`/`.info` porn-spam ring (`cyfar.online`, `yhazu.info`, …).
4. Measure Windows-1250-as-Latin-1 mojibake beyond the strong `è`+`¹` signature (948 docs, 0.05%) — the `»`/`¾` variants suggested a larger tail that I could not separate from legitimate guillemet use.
